note: Rewritten from Sands' (1999) new species description, original in English; the genus lacks soldiers; the species is named after Luc Dibog, a member of the TIGER project, who first recognized it on the basis of the enteric valve and the first hindgut segment.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The first hindgut segment is long and inflated, displacing the enteric valve seat to the dorsolateral left of the abdomen, one of the most easily recognized characters in this genus; the primary-row spines of the enteric valve are fine and the secondary-row scales densely spinulose, unique in the genus. From A. congoensis it differs in having the anterior margin of the third marginal tooth of the left mandible shorter than that of the first marginal tooth and the fourth marginal tooth just touching the lateral edge of the molar prominence. The author considered its differences from the other species of the genus insufficient to erect a new genus.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow or yellow, the darkest part of the antennal flagellum yellow or pale yellowish brown, pronotum yellowish white or pale yellow, legs pale yellow, abdominal tergites transparent. Head capsule circular to oval, setae sparse, projecting, the longest setae more or less regularly and symmetrically arranged. Fontanelle absent. Anterior surface of the fore coxa usually with 4 or more stout setae arranged in rows or groups; fore tibia with 3 distal spurs, the third well developed or far smaller than the other two. Left mandible: first marginal tooth nearly equilateral, anterior margin of the third marginal tooth shorter than that of the first marginal tooth, the fourth marginal tooth just touching the lateral edge of the molar prominence in frontal view; right mandible: anterior margin of the first marginal tooth shorter than that of the second marginal tooth. Measurements: head width 0.656—0.701 mm; pronotum width 0.440—0.489 mm, length 0.192—0.227 mm; hind tibia length 0.659—0.730 mm; fore tibia length 0.576—0.618 mm; left mandible index 0.801—0.902, right mandible index 0.973—1.295.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The midgut–hindgut junction arises ventrally to the left of the nerve cord; the first hindgut segment is very long, more than 8 times as long as its proximal width, inflated throughout to about 2 times the basal width; in the undissected abdomen the enteric valve lies to the left of the heart (dorsal view); the third lobe of the enteric valve seat is nearly as large as the outer pair. The enteric valve ridges are nearly taper-ellipsoid from the base towards the apical spines, unsclerotized or colourless throughout, bearing very long tapering spines, at most about 14, straight and evenly tapering, not wider than the narrowest point of ridge three, nearly six-radiate except for slight differences in ridge size; the secondary rows bear conspicuous spines on one or more ridges.
